turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, Mrs Naidoo. Come through. Your sister's welcome to stay. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, doctor, I'm just so tired all the time. And the periods, they're...
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's finished, hey. At the school she's sitting down between lessons.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I teach grade four. By second break I'm done. Yesterday's concert rehearsal nearly finished me, but that's another story.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the tiredness been going on?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. A while. Maybe since...
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since the bleeding got properly bad. That's what I keep telling her.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The monthlies. They're heavy. About a year, I think. Ja.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Longer. It was already bad before last Christmas. That's a year and a half, easy.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it? I lose track of these things. Ja, maybe.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): So I'll put the heavy bleeding somewhere between a year and eighteen months, and the tiredness sitting alongside it. Tell me what the bleeding is actually like.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I go through pads, lots, six or seven, I don't know, sometimes I change and it's already soaked and I...
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You told me eight on Tuesday.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't count properly, doctor. It depends on the day. Don't write eight like it's exact.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clots?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Big clots. Like a R5 coin, sometimes bigger. Shame, it's embarrassing.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many days does it run?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): It used to be four or five. Now it's more like eight, nine days, and then it stops and...
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Starts again?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Spotting, another couple of days. I think. Not sure it's every month the same. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain with it?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really cramps, not like when I was younger. More just washed out.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): And short of breath?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, walking up to the classroom. Those stairs. I have to stop halfway.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And at the robot last week she pulled over, she said she couldn't...
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): That was once. I sat a minute and I was alright. Don't make a whole story.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain when that happens?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy? Blackouts?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes. Not really. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your sister said something at reception about your hair.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's coming out in the brush. Proper clumps in the shower drain.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, it's thinner. I noticed a few months back. I can't tell you the week. I don't know.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you ever had a thyroid problem yourself?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not that I know of.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Our mom was on tablets her whole life for an underactive thyroid. And aunty Betty had a goitre, they took half of it out in Durban.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mom with underactive thyroid, aunt with a goitre and surgery. Any illnesses of your own, or operations?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Two kids, normal deliveries, no operations. I was on the pill for a bit, that's all.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you still taking that?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): The combined one. I stopped months ago. It made me moody, so I just left it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about iron?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, the red iron tablets. From the chemist. Sometimes.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sometimes meaning?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every day. I forget. When I remember, one in the morning. With rooibos, if that matters.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She skips more than she swallows. The bottle in the kitchen is still almost full.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you know the strength?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I think two hundred milligrams. Or maybe those are the smaller ones. The box is at home. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Red iron tablets, possibly 200 mg, one in the morning when you remember. Did the clinic give you anything else?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): A white tablet, once, for the bleeding. I can't remember the name. It's still...
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you actually take any?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I got scared of the leaflet and left it in the cupboard.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She did take one of my water tablets, though, when her ankles...
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): That was yours, not mine. Once. And the ankles were fine the next day, so leave it.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, we won't put someone else's tablet on your list. Are the ankles swelling now?
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not now.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me look at you. Pale in the inner eyelids and the palms, pulse 96, blood pressure 112 over 74. Chest is clear, heart sounds normal, no murmur, and the tummy is soft with no mass.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Is pale bad?

[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): It fits with the blood loss. I'm not calling it anaemia until the bloods are back. My working thought is the heavy periods are draining you, and with the hair and your mom's thyroid we should check that too, not assume it.
[SEG0059] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Does she need a scan of the womb?
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might arrange a pelvic ultrasound if the bleeding stays this heavy or the bloods don't explain it. I'm not booking it today.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am requesting a full blood count, a ferritin, and thyroid function. And I'll start Cyklokapron, one gram three times a day, only on the heavy days.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Cyklokapron. Is that the white tablet? I don't...
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, different medicine. It helps the lining clot. Take it with food. If you soak a pad every hour for a few hours, or you feel faint, come straight in, don't wait on me.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. And the red tablets?
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep them for now. Try to take one every morning until we see the ferritin, and if you miss a dose don't double up.
[SEG0066] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should she stay off work?

[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not from what I've heard. Pace the stairs, sit if you're breathless. Come back in two weeks for the results. If the bleeding gets heavier before then, don't wait for that appointment.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Ja. I'll forget half of this, I know I will.
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your sister's got the plan with you, and the script will be at reception. We'll see you in two weeks.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Intermenstrual spotting for another couple of days after the 8–9 day period, not the same every month.
She denied significant menstrual cramps/pain, saying not really cramps like when she was younger.
Dizziness/blackouts were asked about and the response was equivocal: sometimes dizzy, but not really; no clear blackouts confirmed.
Past history also included 'two kids, normal deliveries' in addition to no operations.
She had previously been given an unnamed white tablet for the bleeding by the clinic but did not take any because she was scared of the leaflet; this is omitted from medications/history.
Current iron tablet dose is recorded as 200 mg, but in the transcript the patient was unsure whether it was 200 mg.
She once took one of her sister's water tablets; doctor explicitly said not to add someone else's tablet to her medication list.

Doctor's assessment also included possible thyroid contribution and specifically not to assume it: heavy periods likely causing symptoms, but hair loss plus maternal thyroid history means thyroid disease should be checked too.
